concept_use.Angle between two lines: tan(pi/4) = |(m - 3)/(1 + 3m)| gives the two candidate slopes -2 and 1/2.
concept_use.Angle between line and circle: The angle between L and the circle (acute angle with the tangent, radius perpendicular to tangent) gives the distance condition d = r cos(pi/3) = sqrt 5, which selects m = -2.

english: A line $L$ passes through the point $(1,-7)$ and is inclined at an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to the line $3x-y=0$. The line $L$ meets the circle $x^2+y^2=20$, and at each point common to $L$ and the circle, the acute angle between $L$ and the tangent to the circle is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$. If $L$ meets the $x$-axis at $(p,0)$, then the value of $p$ is ______.
hindi: एक रेखा $L$ बिन्दु $(1,-7)$ से होकर जाती है तथा रेखा $3x-y=0$ से कोण $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ पर झुकी है। रेखा $L$ वृत्त $x^2+y^2=20$ से मिलती है, तथा $L$ और वृत्त के प्रत्येक उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दु पर $L$ तथा वृत्त की स्पर्श रेखा के बीच का न्यून कोण $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ है। यदि $L$, $x$-अक्ष से $(p,0)$ पर मिलती है, तो $p$ का मान ______ है।
solution: At a common point $T$, the radius $OT$ is perpendicular to the tangent, so $L$ makes the angle $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ with $OT$; hence the distance of $O$ from $L$ is $d=r\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{2\sqrt5}{2}=\sqrt5$
$m=\frac12$: $L:x-2y-15=0$, $d=\dfrac{15}{\sqrt5}=3\sqrt5>r$, it does not meet the circle
solution_full: Let $m$ be the slope of $L$. The angle with $3x-y=0$ (slope $3$) is $\frac{\pi}{4}$: $\left|\dfrac{m-3}{1+3m}\right|=1$.

Angle between a line and a circle: at a common point $T$, the tangent is perpendicular to $OT$. If the line makes the acute angle $\phi$ with the tangent, it makes $\frac{\pi}{2}-\phi$ with $OT$. The foot $N$ of the perpendicular from $O$ to $L$ gives the right triangle $ONT$ with $OT=r$ and $ON=d=r\cos\phi$ (the angle at $T$ between $TN$ and $TO$ is $\frac{\pi}{2}-\phi$).
Here $r=2\sqrt5$ and $\phi=\frac{\pi}{3}$, so $d=\sqrt5$. By symmetry the angle is the same at both common points.
Case $m=\frac12$: $y+7=\frac12(x-1)$, i.e. $x-2y-15=0$; $d=\dfrac{15}{\sqrt5}=3\sqrt5>2\sqrt5$, so this line does not meet the circle. Rejected.
originality_note: New: the angle at which a line cuts a circle is converted into a distance condition d = r cos(phi), and combined with an angle-between-lines condition that gives two candidate slopes, one of which misses the circle (way 5). Closest known: 'lines through a point inclined at 45 degrees to a given line'. Different because: the circle-intersection angle, not a tangency, decides between the candidates.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Defined the angle between a line and a circle in the stem (acute angle with the tangent at a common point) so there is one reading. Changed: definition added.
key_step: Translating the cutting angle pi/3 into d = r cos(pi/3) and using it to choose between the slopes -2 and 1/2.
justification: Two ideas linked (angle between lines, angle between a line and a circle as a distance condition) with a rejection; the second idea is less practised. Comparable to the L3 coordinate chains (2021-P1-Q1).
